title: E0132: Header injection via header
plain_english: Writing user-controlled input to HTTP headers with `header()` without sanitizing CRLF sequences (`\r\n`) can allow HTTP header injection.
why_matters: Header injection can: - Inject malicious headers such as `Set-Cookie`, `Location`, or `Content-Type` - Enable cache poisoning - Contribute to cross-site scripting (XSS) in some contexts - Bypass security controls that rely on header values
what_it_checks: `header()` calls with tainted input that may contain CRLF sequences
`header()` calls where user input is interpolated into the header value
